evals.prompt: Write a glossary for this repo. Our docs use 'context' for a section of the task file and for the model's context window, and nobody agrees what a 'job' is.
evals.expected_output: States the evidence set as one sentence and asks one question, whether it is complete, before research. Reads every tracked Markdown file, records every usage of the candidates with path and line, and checks the code for the identifiers that carry each word. 'context' fails the entry test's second condition because 'Context section' and 'context window' fit every usage, so it becomes a rename in the glossary report, never an entry for the bare word. 'job' gets an entry only when it passes a gate. Interviews with 2 to 4 options per open decision, each a qualifier or a new word per thing. Shows the complete GLOSSARY.md draft and the reference line '- Read `GLOSSARY.md` first. Use every word it defines with that meaning.' with its place in the root AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, and writes nothing before approval. Writes only GLOSSARY.md and that one line. Finishes with the glossary report: Added, Changed, Removed, Renamed, Facts to place, Instructions, Disagreements.

evals.prompt: Audit GLOSSARY.md. I think half the entries are things nobody would misread.
evals.expected_output: Reads the existing glossary and every usage of each term. For each entry that passes neither Gate A nor Gate B, or that no document uses, asks one question listing each with its gate and failed condition or the word 'unused': remove all, some by name, or none. Definitions that hold a path, placeholder, format, allowed-value list, section list, or condition are reported under Facts to place with the document and line that use them. Rewrites no document itself: each disagreeing usage goes in the report, and the disambiguating-text skill is offered only after the glossary is saved.

evals.prompt: Make a glossary for docs/. Every word in there already has exactly one meaning as far as I can tell.
evals.expected_output: When no word passes Gate A or Gate B, writes no draft and no reference line. Goes to approval with the glossary report alone and asks whether the user confirms an empty glossary. On confirmation, deletes an existing GLOSSARY.md if one exists and writes no new one. Asks nothing else after the report.
